title: The Mathieu property for quadratic complements
summary: Classifies quadratic-complement traces in characteristic zero, proves the joint minima for explicit witnesses and gives a bounded one-order test for all multipliers. It also classifies the real special orthogonal Reynolds projection.
abstract:
For a nondegenerate quadratic form \(q\) of dimension \(N\ge1\) over a
characteristic-zero field, the kernel of the normalized rotation and
scaling trace on \(\{q\ne0\}\) is Mathieu--Zhao exactly when \(N\le2\).
In every higher dimension a single witness attains the minimum pole
order, numerator degree and polynomial multiplier degree, namely
\(1,3,1\). A second witness gives sharp degree cutoffs for its detecting
multipliers. For an arbitrary regular phase, testing finitely many
multipliers at one computable order decides eventual vanishing
against every fixed multiplier. For phases affine in the angular
variable, a Laurent support criterion suffices. Over \(\mathbb R\),
the kernel of the special orthogonal Reynolds projection is
Mathieu--Zhao exactly when \(q\) is definite or \(N\le2\).

verification.scope: Written arguments, bounded exact arithmetic controls, and PDF-only internal review of the exponent shift, the degree bound and the special orthogonal Reynolds classification.
verification.limits: External specialist review, independent external replay, and full formal verification remain pending.
